subject: Control plane proxy reconfiguration — transient disconnect and evidence request
body:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@medisphere.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 06 Oct 2027 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Control plane proxy reconfiguration — transient disconnect and evidence request

Elena,

Thanks for taking the time on the quick call earlier. I wanted to follow up in writing with what we observed from Redwood's side and to request a couple of artifacts that will help us narrow the root cause.

Summary of what we saw (Redwood telemetry):
- 2027-10-06 16:44:12–16:52:37 UTC: a burst of TLS handshake failures between our private control plane proxy fleet and Medisphere agent IPs.
- Failure mode: handshake aborts with "unexpected_message" and some sessions resetting mid-KV-sync.
- About 3.6% of agent connections in the private VPC cluster experienced transient disconnect; most recovered within 90s after reconnect and backoff.
- Impact: short-lived inference errors (503) observed by a subset of hosts; no persisted data loss.

Immediate ask from Redwood: could you share the controlplane-facing proxy logs and a short pcap of an affected host's egress during the window (16:40–16:55 UTC)? That will help us correlate SNI/TLS versions and whether there were retransmits.

What we're doing now (action items):
- We've pinned client routing to the fallback orchestrator endpoint to reduce exposure for the rest of the fleet.
- Collecting server-side TLS debug logs and memory of the proxy process; attaching what we have so far.
- Engaging infra to reproduce proxy rotation in staging with your proxy configuration.

Attachments: controlplane-rotation-20271006-rtlogs.tar.gz (redwood runtime logs trimmed to the window).

Proposed next steps and timeline:
- If you can share the pcap and proxy logs by EOD today (UTC), we'll aim to have a preliminary correlation within 6 hours.
- If helpful, we can schedule a bridge: suggested times 17:30–18:30 UTC.

Sorry for the disruption — we'll keep this high-priority until we have a root cause and a mitigation.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
priom.das@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0127

From: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@medisphere.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Victor Chu <security@medisphere.com>
Date: Wed, 06 Oct 2027 17:03:21 +0000
Subject: Re: Control plane proxy reconfiguration — transient disconnect and evidence request

Priyom —

Thanks for the heads up. We did a quick check on our side and are attaching two files: a condensed proxy log and a short pcap from one of the affected hosts. Our initial observation:
- Proxy rotated a config bundle at ~16:43 UTC as part of an automated rollout.
- Multiple clients logged "tls: unexpected message" followed by TCP RST in close succession.
- Affected hosts are running an older OpenSSL (1.1.1k) due to an internal dependency.

We are attaching the relevant snippets. We will keep the bridge open if you want to jump on.

Attachments: client-pcap-sample.txt (pcap interpreted), medisphere-proxy-condensed.log

— Elena
Elena Ramos
Platform Ops Manager, Medisphere Health
elena.ramos@medisphere.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@medisphere.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 06 Oct 2027 17:28:10 +0000
Subject: Re: Control plane proxy reconfiguration — transient disconnect and evidence request

Elena — thanks for the quick artifacts, that was extremely helpful. Initial correlation notes:
- The pcap shows a pattern where the server completes a TLS ServerHello but then immediately sends a TLS Alert "unexpected_message" on a subset of resumed sessions.
- Our runtime logs show the proxy rotation triggered a mass restart of the proxy workers; in about 40% of restarts the session cache was not gracefully migrated, which exposed clients using session resumption -> causing the handshake to fall back into a failure path on older OpenSSL builds.

Temporary mitigations we've applied on Redwood's side:
- Re-enabled the previous proxy config in the control plane for the affected region and forced session cache warmup.
- Deployed a short-lived traffic-split rule to route 100% of agent control traffic to a stable cluster while we investigate.

Request for permission: with your approval we'd like to capture full proxy debug logs for one rotation cycle (this will increase log verbosity for ~10m). Please confirm and we'll proceed.

I'll set up a shared folder and drop a short correlation CSV once we finish parsing.

— Priyom

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@medisphere.com>, Victor Chu <security@medisphere.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 07 Oct 2027 09:30:00 +0000
Subject: Post-incident update: control plane proxy rotation — preliminary findings and next steps

Elena/Victor —

Thanks again for your cooperation yesterday. Below is a short post-incident summary and the next steps we will take. We will follow up with a formal postmortem doc within 72 hours.

What happened (preliminary):
- During an automated proxy config rollout in your VPC (16:43 UTC 2027-10-06), proxy worker processes were restarted in a way that flushed the in-memory TLS session cache on a subset of instances.
- Agents using session resumption (and older OpenSSL stacks) hit a code path that returned TLS alerts instead of negotiating a fresh handshake, producing transient connection failures and 503 responses at the application layer.

Scope and impact:
- ~3.6% of active agents saw transient errors for an average of 75 seconds; traffic automatically recovered after the retry/backoff.
- No customer data was exposed; this is an availability incident.

Root cause (likely):
- Proxy rotation script did not coordinate session-cache migration across worker restarts. That left a window where resumed sessions negotiated against a worker with an empty cache leading to incorrect TLS alert behavior for some client stacks.

Immediate remediation (already done):
- Rolled back to the previous proxy configuration for the control plane and forced session cache prewarming.
- Added a temporary traffic split routing rule to avoid the affected cluster during verification.

Planned next steps:
- Patch the rollout script to perform in-place reloads that preserve session cache or to use a rolling rebalance with session handoff (ETA: 48 hours).
- Add a Canary run that includes at least one host with older OpenSSL (we will validate handshake paths).
- Provide you with a remediation checklist and a copy of the runtime patch once merged.

Artifacts attached: redwood-controlplane-summary-20271007.pdf (draft), controlplane-rotation-20271006-rtlogs.tar.gz, client-pcap-sample.txt.

References: JIRA SUP-4721 (tracking patch + postmortem), shared Drive folder: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/medisphere/ctrlplane-rotation-20271006

We will follow with a formal postmortem and proposed rollout-changes in the next 72 hours. Please let me know if you want a technical bridge to walk through the pcap/logs — happy to schedule.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
